formNote: A counting sign: two parallel lines. Cosmological readings (Heaven and Earth) are later and interpretive.
summary: Two — the simplest written number, and in thought the sign of polarity and division. Negated as 不二 it names a non-duality that declines to split experience into subject and object, pure and impure, this and that.
placement: In the eye of the right wing, mirroring 不: two foci, one unbroken trajectory weaving around both.

satellites.title: The Dharma-Gate of Non-Duality
satellites.evidence: 不二 renders Sanskrit advaya, “not-two”. In chapter 9, bodhisattvas each define the gate of non-duality; Mañjuśrī says it lies beyond words; Vimalakīrti answers with silence — remembered in the idiom 一默如雷, “one silence, like thunder”.

satellites.title: Not-Two Is Not “One”
satellites.evidence: Vedāntic advaita affirms a single underlying reality, Brahman. Buddhist advaya (不二) rejects paired extremes through dependent arising (緣起) without positing any one substance beneath them.
satellites.caveat: Both words combine a- with a Sanskrit word for “two-ness”; the difference is doctrinal, not etymological.
gaps: Cite a scholarly comparison of Buddhist advaya and Vedāntic advaita.

satellites.title: The Pivot of the Way
satellites.evidence: “Where ‘that’ (彼) and ‘this’ (是) no longer find their opposite — this is called the pivot of the Way.” Zhuangzi’s critique of either-or disputation predates the arrival of Buddhism: an indigenous Chinese resonance with 不二.

checked.note: 彼是莫得其偶，謂之道樞

satellites.title: Without a Second
satellites.evidence: Malay tiada duanya means “peerless, without a second” — a structural echo of “not-two”, though it praises uniqueness rather than naming non-duality. French non-dualité is a modern scholarly term.
gaps: French usage of non-dualité is uncited.
